title: Agentic Insurance Protocol (AIP), draft 0.1
description: Generated from schema.ts and registry.ts. Do not edit by hand.

AipError.description: Error returned in an MCP tool result with `isError: true`, in `structuredContent.error`. PAP errors (`insufficient_scope`, `sign_in_required`, `terms_changed`) keep their PAP form.

lines.description: Product lines the server can quote.

countries.description: Countries where the server's products are sold.

can_conclude.description: True when the server can conclude an agreement inside the agent (`conclude`). False when the customer always finishes on the distributor's own page.

AipSettings.description: Settings object of the extension. A server puts it under `capabilities.extensions["org.openfinancialagent/ofap"]` in its MCP `server/discover` response, and under the same key in the `extensions` field of its PAP `poppy.json`.

AnswerOrigin.description: Who produced the value of an answer.

source_name.description: The third party, by its kind and country, for example "vehicle register (FR)".

AnswerSource.description: Where one answer comes from. `validated_by_customer` is true when the customer confirmed this value before the agent sent it. It is always true when the customer gave the value. An agent MUST NOT set `validated_by_customer` to true when the customer did not validate that answer.

AnswerSources.description: The source of each answer, keyed like `answers`. An agent MUST give a source for each answer, and no source for a key that has no answer. Otherwise the server returns `answers_invalid`.

Answers.description: Answers keyed by property name in `answers_schema`.

AnswersSchema.description:
A JSON Schema (2020-12) object that describes the answers. Each property is one question. AIP adds these keywords to each property:

- `x-collected-by`: a `CollectedBy` value. Default `agent`.
- `x-profile-key`: the key of the matching question in the line profile,   when the question is part of the common core.
- `x-ask`: a short question the agent can ask the customer, in plain words.

validated_at.description: When the customer approved the operation: its `confirmation.confirmed_at`.

AnswersValidation.description: The record that the customer validated a set of answers and their sources: a succeeded `validate_answers` operation. The server keeps it. The agent copies it into `quote` to get binding offers, and into the declaration of an application.

handoff_url.description: Page where the customer finishes the subscription.

pricing.description: The pricing of the offer, unchanged. It MUST be the `pricing` that `quote` returned for `offer_id`.

documents_delivered.description: Documents delivered before this revision was proposed. Every document of the offer with `required_before_commitment: true` MUST be in this list.

withdrawal_period_days.description: Days the customer has to withdraw after conclusion, when the law gives the right.

ApplicationTerms.description: Terms of an application or a conclusion. Every field the law needs as evidence is here, so that a confirmed revision records exactly what the customer accepted.

CheckCapacity.description: In which capacity the agent checks a party.

domain.description: Domain of the seller's website or MCP server.

legal_name.description: Legal name that the seller shows, for example in the legal notice of its website.
Legal name that the seller shows, for example in the legal notice of its website.

CheckSubject.description: The party to check. Give a domain, a register entry, or both.

legal_name.description: Legal name, from the AIP server of the domain or from the register.

lei.description: Legal entity identifier, from the AIP server of the domain or from the register.

domain_link.description: How the registry tied the domain to the entries. Present when the params give a domain.

listed.description: True when the registry lists an AIP server on the domain.

mcp_url.description: MCP endpoint of the listed server.

CheckedSubject.description: What the registry found about the party it checked.

CollectedBy.description:
Who collects the value of a question.
- `agent`: the agent MAY ask and send the value.
- `distributor_page`: the value MUST NOT pass through the agent. The customer   gives it on the distributor's own page. Use it for identity numbers, bank   account and card numbers, tax numbers, health details and passwords.

ConcludeResult.description: Result of `conclude`. The operation MUST have `user_approval_required: true`. When it succeeds, `result.data` holds a `ConcludeOutcome`.

ConformanceLevel.description:
Conformance level that a distributor declares.

- 1 Inform: `get_distributor`, `list_products`, `get_documents`
- 2 Quote: level 1, plus `get_question_set`, `quote` and `validate_answers`
- 3 Subscribe: level 2, plus `submit_application` or `conclude`

A server that declares a level MUST implement every tool of that level and of the levels below it, except that level 3 needs only one of `submit_application` and `conclude`. A server at level 2 can give binding offers, because it implements `validate_answers`.

channels.description: Channels the distributor MAY use to contact the customer. Empty means none.

details_collected_by.description: When `distributor_page`, the contact details never pass through the agent.

providers_may_contact.description: True only when the customer agreed that providers may contact them too.

purposes.description: Purposes the customer agreed to, for example "this_application", "marketing".

ContactConsent.description: The customer's choice about later contact.

ConversationData.description: PROPOSED. Some distributors expose only a company agent. If AIP accepts them at level 2, each message that carries an AIP object puts it here, in the message's structured data (`data` in a PAP conversation, `structuredContent` in a chat tool).

CountryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, upper case.

reimbursement_rate.description: Share of a claim paid back, from 0 to 1. Used by pet and health cover.

main_exclusions.description: Main exclusions. The full list is in the documents.

DateTimeString.description: Date and time with offset, ISO 8601.

Decimal.description: A decimal number as a string, so that no value is lost to floating point, for example "12.90".

answer_sources.description: Where each answer comes from, keyed like `answers`.

accuracy_confirmed.description: True when the customer confirmed that the answers are true and complete. The agent MUST NOT set it to true for invented or test data.

validation.description: The customer's validation of these answers and sources. Its hashes MUST be `answers_sha256` and `answer_sources_sha256`, and its operation MUST have succeeded. Otherwise the server returns `answers_not_validated`.

Declaration.description: The answers the customer commits to, with their sources and the customer's validation.

DistributorRole.description: Role of a party in the distribution chain. The provider roles are in `ProviderRole`.

DomainLink.description: How the registry tied a domain to register entries.

DomainName.description: Host name, lower case, with no scheme, port or path, for example "pets.example.com".

answer_sources_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of the answer sources. The server MUST keep the sources with the declaration.

validation.description: The customer's validation of the answers and their sources.

underwriting_scope_version.description: Version of the underwriting scope that the offer applied.

terms_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of the confirmed `terms`.

EvidenceRecord.description:
What the distributor keeps when an operation succeeds. It links the exact revision the customer accepted to the documents, the declaration with its sources and its validation, the needs assessment, the consent and the underwriting scope. The distributor MUST keep it for the period the law requires.

A PAP confirmation proves that an agent stated the customer approved a revision. It does not prove that the customer saw the terms. This record adds what was delivered and what was declared. It still does not prove that the customer read the documents.

countries.description: Countries the product covers. At least one.

subdivisions.description: Subdivisions the product covers, for example US states. Each one MUST belong to a country in `countries`. The product covers the whole of each country that has no subdivision in this list.

Geography.description: Where the insured person lives, or where the insured good is.

subdivision.description: Adds the file of this subdivision, when one exists.

line.description: Adds the file of this line in the country, when one exists.

GetCountryRulesResult.description:
Result of `get_country_rules`.

- `files` MUST start with the file of the country. The file of the   subdivision and then the file of the line follow, when they exist.
- Each file MUST be the same text as the file of the same version in the   skill, so that `sha256` is the same in both places.
- An agent MUST follow every file of the result. When the registry does not   answer, the agent uses the copy in its installed skill, and SHOULD tell the   customer which version it used.

complaints_url.description: Where a customer can complain. Required by most regulators.

Offer.description:
One priced offer. A distributor can return several offers: one per tier, per provider, or per duration.

When a server implements `quote`, an agent MUST take the price, the cover, the limits and the excess that it shows the customer from the offer, and MUST NOT take them from a page made for people.

revision.description: Starts at 1. Increases when the terms change. Only the latest revision can be confirmed.

summary.description: Plain-language terms that the customer can decide from alone.

user_approval_required.description: When true, a standing permission is not enough. The customer MUST approve this revision.

aip_progress.description: AIP reason why the operation is `in_progress`. Not a PAP field. Clients that do not know AIP ignore it.

Operation<ApplicationTerms>.description:
A PAP operation. This mirrors the PAP operations extension (version 1). PAP is the authority for every field here except `terms` and `aip_progress`. When the two differ, PAP wins.

An MCP tool returns it in `structuredContent.operation`. The agent confirms it at the PAP operations endpoint, never through an AIP tool.

QuoteParams.description:
Params of `quote`.

The agent MAY send partial answers. The server then returns `needs_input` with the missing fields, and the agent calls `quote` again with more answers. This one loop replaces the multi-step flow tools (`action`, `stateUpdates`, `sessionId`) that most servers use. Some servers already work this way.

Without `validation`, every offer is indicative. To get binding offers, the agent first has the customer validate the answers with `validate_answers`, then sends the same answers and sources with that `validation`.

To read a quote that is still in progress, send only `quote_request_id`.

missing_fields.description: Properties of `answers_schema` that are missing or not valid.

retry_after_seconds.description: When the agent SHOULD read the quote again.

RegistryError.description:
Error returned in an MCP tool result with `isError: true`, in `structuredContent.error`.

A registry tool MUST refuse a call with a param that this file does not define, and MUST NOT keep its value. That is how the registry stays free of customer data.

RegistrySettings.description:
Settings object of the registry extension. The registry puts it under `capabilities.extensions["org.openfinancialagent/registry"]` in its MCP `server/discover` response.

The registry SHOULD also serve the buyer skill through the MCP Skills extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`). An agent whose host loads skills over MCP then gets the whole skill from the registry, and `get_country_rules` serves the same country files to the other agents.

RegistryToolSignatures.description: Params and result type of each registry tool.

line.description: Present for the file of a line.

reviewed_at.description: Date of the last legal review. Omit when no review happened.

RulesFile.description: One rules file of the buyer skill. The file is Markdown with a YAML front matter. The front matter holds `country`, `version`, `owner`, `status`, and `endorsed_by` and `reviewed_at` when they apply, with the same values as the fields of this object. It also holds `subdivision` and `line` for a file of a subdivision or of a line.

subdivision.description: Subdivision where the customer buys, for example a US state.

insured_family.description: Family of the insured, as in the underwriting scope of a product, for example "pet" or "dwelling".

min_conformance_level.description: Return only servers of this level or above.

SearchDistributorsParams.description: Params of `search_distributors`. The params describe a market, never a person.

SearchDistributorsResult.description:
Result of `search_distributors`.

- Each server in `distributors` MUST match every param of the search: the   country is in its `countries`, the line is in its `lines`, the subdivision   is in its `subdivisions` when it has some, the insured family is in its   `insured_families`, and its level is not below `min_conformance_level`.
- The registry MUST return every listed server that matches, across the   pages.
- The order carries no meaning. The registry MUST NOT rank a server for a   payment or for any commercial link. It SHOULD shuffle the order for each   new search, and keep that order across the pages of the same search.
- An agent MUST NOT show the order to the customer as a ranking.
- A search result is not a licence check. An agent checks the seller with   `verify_licence` before it sends any of the customer's answers.

SessionRequirement.description: Session that a tool needs (PAP draft 0.2).

SourceAccess.description: How the registry reads a public register.

SubdivisionCode.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code, upper case, for example "US-CA" for California.

SubmitApplicationResult.description: When the operation succeeds, `result.data` holds an `ApplicationOutcome`.

SubscriptionPath.description: How a customer can subscribe to a product.

ToolSignatures.description: Params and result type of each tool.

version.description: Version of the scope. A change in any part MUST change it.

insured.description: What the product insures. At least one.

conditions.description: The conditions that a machine cannot check, in plain words, for example "Houses built after 1950 only" or "Not for people over 70". Empty when there are none. An agent SHOULD check them against what the customer said before it quotes, and ask the customer when it is not sure.

UnderwritingScope.description:
The risks a product can cover. `list_products` gives it with no customer data, so that an agent can drop a product that cannot cover the customer before it asks a question.

`geography` and `insured` are the structured part, which a machine can check against the answers. A server MUST NOT return an offer for a risk outside the structured part. An agent MUST NOT send answers to `quote` for a product whose structured part excludes the customer. `conditions` holds the rest.

answer_sources.description: Where each answer comes from, keyed like `answers`.

ValidateAnswersParams.description: Params of `validate_answers`. The agent calls it before it asks for binding offers, and before an application. The answers MUST be complete for the question set. Otherwise the server returns `answers_invalid`.

ValidateAnswersResult.description: Result of `validate_answers`. The operation MUST have `user_approval_required: true`, because only the customer can validate their answers. The agent MUST ask the person who will be the subscriber to approve it. When it succeeds, `result.data` holds a `ValidationOutcome`.

answers_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of `answers`.

answer_sources_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of `answer_sources`.

ValidationTerms.description: Terms of a validation: the answers that the customer validates, and their sources. The `summary` of the operation MUST show each answer and its source in plain words, so that the customer can check each one.

subdivision.description: Subdivision where the customer buys. REQUIRED for a country in `PER_SUBDIVISION_COUNTRIES`, such as the United States.

VerifyLicenceParams.description:
Params of `verify_licence`. The params name a company and a market, never a person.

The check MUST work for a seller that the registry does not list. An agent can find a seller anywhere on the web, and the check matters most then.

check_id.description: Identifier of this check, set by the registry.

params.description: The params of the call, so that the result is a complete record alone.

licences.description: Every entry the registry read for the party.

checked_at.description: When the registry gave the verdict.

VerifyLicenceResult.description:
Result of `verify_licence`.

The registry tests each entry in this order. An entry covers the question when it passes all five tests: 1. Country: the entry exists, and its `country` is the country asked or its    `passports` include it. 2. Subdivision: it has no `subdivisions`, or they include the subdivision    asked. 3. Line: it has no `lines`, or no line is asked, or its `lines` include the    line. 4. Role: for the capacity "provider", its role is a provider role. 5. Status: its status is "active".

The verdict:
- "licensed" when at least one entry covers the question and, if the params   give a domain, `domain_link` is not "not_linked".
- "unknown" when no entry covers the question and the registry could not   read every register that applies, or could not identify the party. Also   when an entry covers the question but the domain is not linked to it.
- "not_licensed" in every other case: the registry read every register that   applies, and no entry covers the question. The reason comes from the entry   that passed the most tests, and names the first test it failed: country   "no_entry", subdivision "subdivision_not_covered", line   "line_not_covered", role "role_not_covered", status "name_mismatch" or   "licence_not_active".

Rules for the registry:
- `licences` MUST list every entry that the registry read for the party in   the registers that apply, including the entries that are not active.
- A verdict MUST rest only on reads made at most `MAX_READ_AGE_DAYS` days   before `checked_at`. The registry SHOULD read the register again for each   call when the register has an API or a web page.
- The registry SHOULD keep each result under its `check_id` for at least five   years, so that it can confirm later what it said.

Rules for the agent:
- An agent MUST check the seller, in the capacity "distributor", with the   customer's country, before it sends any of the customer's answers to that   seller. It MUST give the subdivision where licences apply per subdivision,   and SHOULD give the line.
- An agent MUST check the provider of an offer, in the capacity "provider",   before it applies or concludes, when the provider is not the seller.
- On "not_licensed", the agent MUST NOT send the customer's answers to that   party, and MUST NOT apply or conclude through it. It MUST tell the customer   why.
- On "unknown", the agent MUST tell the customer that the licence could not be   checked, and why. It MUST NOT apply or conclude, and SHOULD NOT send the   customer's answers. It MAY ask the seller for its register identifier and   check again.
- An agent MUST keep each result that it relies on with the record of the   sale, and SHOULD give the customer a copy.
